Directions: Based on the passage below and on your knowledge of social studies, answer each question that follows.
Content: ... What were people using all the extra energy for? More heating and cooking, to be sure, and more travel in steamships and trains; but mainly, people were manufacturing more things: more textiles, more machines, more food and ale, more paper. The pattern was clear: the more you produced, the more energy you needed. And conversely [in reverse], the more energy you used, the more things you produced — and the wealthier you or, more likely, your employer or the state, became.

`text(One)` might just as well relabel [rename] the expanding Industrial Revolution the energy revolution, because the industrial economies of the `text(nineteenth century)` simply could not have developed without the parallel emergence of energy economies to sustain them. And as industrialization spread, country by country, region by region, so did demand for energy. ...
